bug_semantics: Bandit.Headers.get_content_length/1 (historically HTTP1Request.get_header/2) used List.keyfind/3, which returns only the first Content-Length header and silently ignores additional Content-Length lines. RFC 9110 §5.3 / RFC 9112 §6.3 require treating duplicate singleton Content-Length as an unrecoverable framing error. Bandit already rejected comma-separated Content-Length: 0, 43 when values differed, but the multi-line form never reached that check. Combined with HTTP/1 keepalive, leftover body bytes are dispatched as a second pipelined request. Behind a CL-last proxy this is classic CL.CL request smuggling (CWE-444): an unauthenticated client can smuggle a request past edge WAF/ACL/rate-limit/audit that the proxy already applied.
flaw_origin: First-wins Content-Length lookup was first written in e5270b1b19e9f3574aa0f87ec76851d66c38c0af ('Add content-length based body reading'). That commit added defp get_header/3 via List.keyfind(headers, header, 0) and used it to set body_size from the first content-length value, then read that many body bytes. Immediate parent d5989c8d8a806639c73d4294762192a7aba3c3ac accumulated headers but did not look up content-length or read a sized body (read_req_body was a TODO returning empty). 422651d03b6eb5b2fb10d1ace804880389e7132a later moved the same get_header/keyfind-first pattern into lib/bandit/headers.ex get_content_length/1 and added comma-separated duplicate-value rejection, preserving first-wins for multi-line headers. f2ca636eb6df385219957e8934e9fc6efa1630d1 is the first commit that rejects more than one content-length header.
